description:
You are a constitutional law professor organizing your Jurism library for an upcoming course. Your library contains several landmark Supreme Court cases and law review articles. You need to tag each reference by legal doctrine so you can quickly filter them for different lecture topics.

Add the following tags to the specified references in your Jurism library:

1. Brown v. Board of Education — add tags: "equal protection" and "education law"
2. Miranda v. Arizona — add tags: "criminal procedure" and "Fifth Amendment"
3. New York Times Co. v. Sullivan — add tags: "First Amendment" and "defamation"
4. Gideon v. Wainwright — add tags: "Sixth Amendment" and "right to counsel"
5. The Path of the Law (by Holmes) — add tags: "legal theory" and "jurisprudence"

To add tags to an item: click on the item in the center pane to select it, then look at the right-hand info pane. Click the "Tags" tab, then click the "Add" button to add a new tag. Type the tag name exactly as specified above and press Enter to confirm. Repeat for each tag on each item.

All tag names must match exactly as written above (case does not matter). Each of the 5 items should end up with exactly 2 tags.
